title: Interleaved regional cutover with per-request SLO budgeting and session-coherent handoff
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a controlled, interleaved active-active cutover that shifts traffic across regions by consuming per-request SLO budgets and preserving streaming session coherence. This ticket defines the playbook, configuration knobs, and implementation tasks for the gateway/edge layer to: 1) route requests by per-request SLO budget, 2) perform incremental traffic shifts (interleaved windowing) instead of bulk region drains, 3) preserve token continuity for streaming sessions via lightweight session proxies and KV-cache checkpointing, and 4) apply region-local circuit breakers and graded load-shedding to maintain SLOs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Cutover can shift up to 100k req/min across regions without increasing 95th latency breach counts by more than 10% vs baseline.
2) Streaming sessions preserve token continuity for >= 99.95% of resumed streams during cutover windows.
3) Circuit breaker trips result in graceful shedding (reject or downgrade) with documented fallbacks and no session corruption.
4) Playbook validated in canary (eu-west -> us-west) with two successful dry runs and one full failover rehearsal.
5) Metrics, dashboards, and alerts added in Console: per-region SLO burn rate, session-resume success, circuit trips, and KV checkpoint lag.
implementation_notes: High-level design: 1) Per-request SLO Budgeting: compute a dynamic budget bucket per request class (chat-stream, chat-nonstream, embeddings, reranking). The routing layer consults budget controller that exposes a per-region 'available-SLO-units' metric. Traffic shifts consume units; when a region's budget approaches zero, routing proportion is reduced. 2) Interleaved windowing: instead of draining region A then B, the controller moves fixed windows (e.g., 1% every 30s) across sessions while monitoring burn rate. 3) Session coherence: streaming connections are anchored to a lightweight session-proxy layer that can attachment-migrate socket tokens to new region anchors. For stateful model KV cache, use checkpoint+delta replication: write KV snapshot to object store and stream deltas to target region prior to cutover window; resume reads consult checkpoint + on-demand delta fetch. 4) Circuit breakers: three-tier breaker per region (latency, error-rate, headroom). Each tier maps to a graded action: soft-shed (deprioritize batch/low-priority requests), hard-shed (reject non-critical requests with 429 + Retry-After), full-failover (reroute remaining traffic to other regions). 5) Load-shedding policy: policy engine uses request classification with priority label (high | normal | low) and cost-estimate score (context tokens + expected generation). Low-priority long-context requests are queued or rejected during high burn. 6) Observability: add counters for per-request SLO units consumed, session migration rate, KV checkpoint lag, and per-region circuit state. 7) Rollout: feature-flagged via runtime config, gated for Dedicated customers initially, then hosted API general availability.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Strong consistency for KV cache across regions is expensive; we choose eventual-consistent checkpoints with on-demand delta fetch to balance latency. This may cause a small fraction of resumed sessions to see truncated prefix (we will log and surface as <session-resume-truncation>).
- Anchoring sessions with proxies increases a hop and slight latency overhead (~3-7ms P50). Tradeoff accepted for correctness during cutover.
- Per-request SLO budgeting adds complexity to routing; ensures SLO stability but can cause suboptimal cost if budgets are conservative.
- Circuit breaker sensitivity needs tuning; overly-sensitive breakers will shed healthy traffic. We'll iterate with canary experiments.
- Security: session token migration must be signed and expiry-limited; security review required (see security_review_required = true).
runbook:
Pre-cutover checklist:
- Ensure KV checkpoint pipeline healthy and last_checkpoint_age < 60s for target region.
- Confirm SLO budgets are at baseline and no active incidents.
- Start small interleaved window: 0.5% every 30s for first 10min, monitor burn.
- Canary verification steps: validate streaming resume on 5 synthetic sessions per window, check 95th latency and error-rate.
Abort path:
- If per-region 95th latency breach > 20% or session-resume success < 99% in two consecutive windows, abort and revert routing to previous steady-state.
Post-cutover validation:
- Run a 1-hour stability window with telemetry checks; if all pass, increase window size and finalize cutover.
monitoring_and_alerts:
Dashboards: region-slo-burn, per-request-class-routing-weight, session-resume-rate, kv-checkpoint-lag.
Alerts: P0 if session-resume-rate < 99.5% for 5m; P0 if region-slo-burn-rate > 150% of baseline for 5m; P1 if circuit-breaker enters hard-shed for >2m and affects >5% traffic.
PRs and dashboards: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-router/pull/452
Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/edge-cutover/region-slo-burn
security_considerations:
- Session tokens must be rotated and signed; migration tokens have single-use semantics with 30s TTL.
- KV checkpoint artifacts encrypted at rest (KMS) during replication.
- Access audits for cutover controllers and playbook steps (console actions) must be logged to audit trail.
- Require formal security review before enabling default for hosted API.
tasks: Implement per-request SLO budget controller and API
Add routing hook to consult budget controller and apply interleaved windowing
Build session-proxy lightweight anchor and token-migration protocol
KV checkpoint + delta streamer to object store with region replication
Circuit breaker: latency/error/headroom tiers and graded shedding actions
Integrate metrics into Console and build dashboards/alerts
End-to-end canary tests and rehearsal runbook
